subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@finapp.com>, Tom Wu <tom.wu@finapp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-12T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we’re aligned. Feel free to correct anything I’ve missed.

Pain points and goals
- Cost: current spend on proprietary APIs (OpenAI + Anthropic) is high; goal is ~40% unit cost reduction while preserving quality.
- Predictability: bursty traffic causing budget overruns; need committed/dedicated capacity options for peak times.
- Compatibility: many existing prompts, safety tooling, and function-calling integrations built against OpenAI/Anthropic semantics — migration must be minimally disruptive.
- Compliance & data residency: logs/eval storage must meet FinApp security controls; need SOC 2 and network diagram for procurement.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Primary: OpenAI for chat/completion (davinci/gpt-4 style).
- Secondary: Anthropic for safety and some classification tasks.
- Infra: requests proxied through a gateway (internal platform) with per-request metadata; some tooling relies on OpenAI-compatible function calls.
- Volume: ~1B tokens/month (peak windows during batch runs).

Success criteria (what FinApp needs to consider a win)
- Latency: P95 end-to-end token latency under ~300ms for typical interactive flows.
- Quality: parity or better on our 10k prompt eval set (metrics: top-1 intent accuracy, hallucination rate).
- Cost: >=40% reduction in per-token cost for steady-state workload.
- Ops: ability to pin model versions, roll back, and get transparent token-level cost breakdowns.

Compatibility needs / blockers
- API compatibility: function-calling and streaming behavior; want minimal prompt refactors.
- Safety: need same or better safety filter integration and audit logs.
- Data: option to keep KV cache and audit logs in customer-controlled storage (VPC).

Model shortlist (initial)
- Llama 2 / 70B (quantized variants) — good latency/cost tradeoff with tuning.
- Mistral / Mixtral variants — promising for instruction-following tasks.
- RedPajama / MPT family for embeddings and lighter gen tasks.

Next steps (agreed)
1) I’ll share: compatibility checklist, initial MA (master agreement) template, and a sample prompt set for your evals (attached).
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra and security teams next week (30–45m) — please propose times.
3) We’ll run a 2-week eval on a representative slice of traffic to measure latency/quality/cost.
4) You’ll share any additional compliance/contract requirements for procurement (SOC2 evidence, network diagram).

Attachments: redwood-ddc-compatibility-checklist.xlsx, redwood-initial-ma-template.docx, finapp-sample-prompt-set.jsonl

Appreciate the candid session — I’ll follow up with proposed slots for the deep-dive.

Best,
Rishi
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
+rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
From: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@finapp.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Wu <tom.wu@finapp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-12T17:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Thanks Rishi — this looks accurate and really helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- Volumes: our current average is ~1B tokens/month, but more importantly we have 2 weekly batch jobs that create significant peak load (30–45m windows).
- Latency: 300ms p95 is our target for interactive flows; for batch jobs we care more about throughput and cost.
- Safety: we use Anthropic for a downstream calibration/safety pass on a subset of responses; preserving that hook (or an equivalent) is required.
- Integrations: our orchestration expects OpenAI-style streaming + function call semantics; breaking changes here add ~3–4 weeks of engineering work.

On next steps:
- We can do a technical deep-dive on Wednesday 3/18 at 10:00am PT or Thursday 3/19 at 2:00pm PT — both work for infra and security.
- Procurement will need SOC 2 Type II report and your standard data-processing addendum.
- Please include a rough cost model for the 2-week eval and a sample SLO/rollout plan in your follow-up.

One more ask: can you share any prior migration notes where customers preserved function-call compatibility with minimal prompt changes? That will help our platform team estimate effort.

Thanks —
Sarah Jones
Director, AI Integrations
FinApp
+sarah.jones@finapp.com
